title: A MORNING PRAYER: I COMMIT THIS DAY TO YOU — LET YOUR PLANS PREVAIL
text: You did not wake yourself up. Something signed for you to see this day. >> [music] >> Somewhere in the courts of heaven, a decision was made that you would not be a statistic, that you would not be a memory, that you would still be standing here present, breathing, positioned. Before you ask God for one more thing, stop and receive [music] that. You are not here by accident, you are here by appointment. And because you are here by appointment, this day [music] is not neutral. This day was not manufactured by the sun rising in the east. [music] This day is a vessel, and what gets poured into it is still, even now, being decided. That is why I will not let [music] this morning pass as ordinary. I refuse to let it slide by as one more square on a calendar. Something in me says today carries weight [music] that yesterday did not carry. And if you will lean in with me, if you will lift your hands where you are, and let your spirit come to attention, I believe before we are done here, heaven will have said something over your life that changes the temperature of everything you are walking into. [music] I hear the spirit saying there is a company of people who have been managing their days instead of consecrating them. You have been surviving mornings instead of surrendering them. You wake up, you check the time, you check your phone, you check the noise of the world before you have checked in with the one who owns the day. And so your day starts on somebody else's terms, on the terms of a headline, a message, a demand, a fear. Instead of starting on the terms of the God who scripted eternity before he scripted your Tuesday. This morning, [music] we are not doing that. This morning, we are going to do something ancient and something powerful in the [music] same breath. We are going to commit this day to the Lord. Psalm 90:12 says, "So teach us to number our days >> [music] >> that we may apply our hearts onto wisdom. Number your days." Not just count them, number them, weigh them, value them, [music] because a day that is not numbered is a day that is wasted and a life is nothing but a collection of days. >> [music] >> So, a wasted day is a wasted portion of destiny you will never recover. There is no refund policy on time. Heaven does not run a returns counter for misused mornings. >> [music] >> That is why the wise man did not pray for more days. He prayed for a heart that knew what to do with the days he already had. Proverbs 16:3 says, "Commit thy works unto the Lord and [music] thy thoughts shall be established." This is not a suggestion. It is a spiritual mechanism. When you commit your works, not just your worship, not just your Sunday, but your works, your plans, your meetings, your decisions, your assignments, when you commit those to the Lord, something happens to your thoughts. They become established. They stop wobbling. They stop being tossed by every wind of anxiety and second-guessing. >> [music] >> A mind that is anchored in a committed day becomes a mind that cannot be easily shaken because it is no longer carrying the day alone.
